title: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO): 2026 Guide
summary: Generative engine optimization (GEO) is how you get cited by ChatGPT, Perplexity & Google AI. The complete 2026 guide: tactics, tools & metrics.
body_markdown:
GEO and answer engine optimization (AEO) describe the same practice. "AI visibility" is the umbrella term. Whatever you call it, the job is the same: become the answer, not just a result.


## What is generative engine optimization?


GEO is a set of on-page, off-page, and technical practices that increase the odds an AI engine cites you when it composes an answer. It overlaps heavily with SEO (AI retrieves from the web, so strong SEO feeds GEO), but it adds new priorities: extractable answers, schema, fact density, corroboration, and crawler access.


## Why does GEO matter in 2026?


**Because a growing share of buyer research now ends inside an AI answer that names only a few brands.** Interest in the term has grown explosively. Search demand for answer engine optimization has risen dramatically year over year. The discovery surface is shifting from ten blue links to a single composed answer, and GEO is how you stay visible on it.


On average, AI engines name only 2-4 brands per buying query (far fewer than the 10 blue links on a traditional search results page), making inclusion in the answer set substantially more valuable.


## GEO vs AEO vs SEO: what's the difference?


**SEO targets rankings in link lists; AEO/GEO target citations inside AI answers.** They share foundations (authority, structure, quality) but diverge in what they optimize for. Full breakdown:[AEO vs GEO vs SEO explained](https://siftly.ai/blog/aeo-vs-geo-vs-seo-explained) .


## How do you do generative engine optimization? (the core tactics)


1. **Answer-first content** : lead every page with a direct, extractable answer.
2. **Question-based structure** : headings phrased as buyer questions; cover the sub-questions (query fan-out).
3. **Schema markup** : FAQ, How-To, Article, and more so models can parse you.
4. **Fact density** : specific, dated, sourced numbers get cited.
5. **Earn corroboration** : be in the trusted third-party lists AI reads.
6. **Open crawler access** : allow GPTBot, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended.
7. **Freshness** : update content and dates regularly.
8. **Measure & iterate** : track mentions and citations, then improve.


Deep dives:[answer engine optimization guide](https://siftly.ai/blog/aeo-prompts-optimization-guide) ,[optimize for AI Overviews](https://siftly.ai/blog/aeo-in-product-searching) ,[optimize content for LLMs](https://siftly.ai/blog/how-to-optimize-content-for-llms) , and the printable[GEO checklist](https://siftly.ai/blog/geo-checklist-content-optimization) .


## How do you measure GEO success?


Track mention rate, share of voice, citation rate, and sentiment across engines, the same metrics covered in our[AI brand monitoring](https://siftly.ai/blog/ai-brand-monitoring) and[AI citation tracking](https://siftly.ai/blog/ai-citation-tracking) guides.[Siftly's GEO content tools](https://siftly.ai/features/geo-content) help you produce content structured to win citations.


## Is SEO dead because of GEO?


**No, SEO is an input to GEO, not a casualty of it.** AI retrieves from the web, so the pages that rank well are often the ones that get cited. We unpack this in[is SEO dead with AI?](https://siftly.ai/blog/is-seo-dead-with-ai) .
